357.body: September form: cost-to-go credit (definition). The addressed-attention model samples four hard trajectories, each a chain of decisions (read, key, emit). The old estimator credited every parameter event with the loss of the whole trajectory. The new one credits an event with the cost that follows it, measured from its next cross-entropy boundary, minus a baseline taken from the other three trajectories. Schematically, for decision \(t\) of trajectory \(i\), \[\hat g^{(i)}_t=\Big(G^{(i)}_t-\bar G^{(-i)}_t\Big)\,s^{(i)}_t,\qquad G^{(i)}_t=\sum_{u\ge t}c^{(i)}_u,\] with \(c\) the per-boundary cost and \(s\) the recorded score of the parameter event (the exact normalisation is in the source). October form: unified credit (definition). The saved native model (called saved437) scores relations between H4 elements (the 120 vertices of the 600-cell, a four-dimensional shape) and Generate prototypes . The unified fit computes independent conditional utilities over all 120 H4 elements. It restores the saved fractional masters, whose served form is quarter-step codes \(q/4\) with \(q\in\{-7,\dots,7\}\). It then fits the context carriers, the prototypes and the coefficients together on the pooled-ranking plus end-of-reply objective. A lane reads at most 120 encountered prototypes. Whole-path design (hypothesis). Extend credit to compiler spans, exact store writes, E8 root choices and consumed donors through an explicit graph of hard decisions. Exact token, occurrence and version identity stay separate from the geometric summaries. Shared writer (definition). One learned vector table encodes the input token, ranks the output and carries the compiler/store/emitter channel. Tokens get a product cell from the root numbers of their first and last 8-dimensional block, and a target omitted from the shortlist still receives score credit. Rule check. The sampled-choice credit used by the whole-path producer uses softmax, so it is blocked by D23, and the pooled-ranking loss used softplus. The shared-writer margin form and the integer writer are compliant. No dense matrix multiplication is needed (D30): the finite factors use table reads and quarter-step sums, and 31 vendor-boundary controls passed for the writer. The served M2 form is already integer (D11), but the export gap of the unified form was never measured, and every position still scores all 4,096 answer choices, so per-token access is not sparse. D37 allows a float re-registration with a fresh review, an owner release, a scanned module and a reported export gap.

365.body: Write each fact once, under an exact address, and read it back exactly. Do not smear it across weights, and do not hunt for it by fuzzy similarity. The address is built from prime numbers: every word has its own prime, so the same words always name the same slot. A new value replaces the old one, but the old one stays recoverable. A fact that was never written can answer "I do not know". In the one probe that checked, the store was never the cause of a failure: among 1,905 held-out misses, none was an eviction or a wrong stored value. What failed was the model's learned step of forming the address from a question.

366.body: The key-value memory. A transformer keeps a key and a value for every earlier word and finds the right one by comparing the question against all the keys. Here the question is turned into an address instead, and the address is looked up directly. No comparison against every key is needed. A conversation scrolling past a row of numbered slots. Each stated fact writes a tile labelled with a product of two primes, and a correction stacks a new version on the old tile. A question lights the matching tile and its latest version. An unwritten key shows Absent and an overwritten slot shows Evicted. Beside it, a bar chart of one test: perfect when the address is right, near zero on new phrasing, perfect again when the address is supplied. Left, how a fact is written, corrected and read, with the two honest failure answers. Right, why the tested models failed: the store was fine, the address was not formed.

366.title: What it replaces in a transformer

367.body: Three built forms share one idea. In each, the address is exact. 1. Exact log and prime sieve (measurement on fixtures; the gcd arithmetic itself is proof). Every user turn is logged as word atoms. Each word has a prime from a registry table. A clause's address is the product \(A_c=\prod_{p\in S_c}p\) over its set \(S_c\) of distinct content primes, plus its ordered pairs of neighbours (n-lets). A query \(q\) is built the same way. A clause is admitted when \[\gcd(q, A_c) > 1,\] that is, when they share at least one prime. The greatest common divisor is computed as a sorted merge of the two factor lists, so no division is needed. Ranking is a separate step: most shared primes first, then latest occurrence, then ordered-pair match. A record counts as evicted only when its ring slot was actually overwritten. 2. The exact relation store (AERM, "G v1"). Learned heads tag each token as entity, relation, value or other. An integer store maps (entity, relation) to a value. It also keeps the previous distinct value and a version counter. A read answers one of four ways for the current and the previous version: None, Hit, Absent or Evicted. A prime-route variant keys by the semiprime \(k=p_a p_b\) of two atoms. By unique factorization (proof), \(k\) names the unordered pair exactly. The value is routed through the expert so that direction survives. 3. Product-key memory. The query splits into two halves. Each half is scored against \(S\) sub-keys and the top \(k\) on each side are kept. That gives \(k^2\) candidate slots, scored by the sum \(s_1(i)+s_2(j)\). The best \(k\) slots are read from an \(S\times S\) table. With \(S=256\) the table has 65,536 rows and a token reads 32 of them. The sub-keys are learned, or fixed to the 120 unit icosians or the 240 E8 roots. The built form mixes the rows with softmax weights. Rule check. Rule Verdict for the exact log, sieve and store Verdict for the tested trained forms No softmax anywhere (D23) Clean Broken. The product-key form mixes rows with softmax, and the tag and trigger heads trained with cross-entropy No matrix multiplication (D30) Clean Not clean. They sit inside a dense float stack Integer-only serving (D11) Fits by design, but nothing is built. The integer serving crate has no gcd, and it refuses product-key memory No served form Discrete path (D32) and offline float (D37) The integer store matches the discrete shape. No memory store exists in the discrete crate yet A learned tagger would be float with an integer export and a reported gap. No hold is released D23 bans softmax. D11 fixes the served form as integer and table lookups. D37 allows float in offline training only. D30 (no matrix multiplication) is in the same file.

375.body: This is storage, not thinking. It keeps data exactly, so a chat memory can be saved, checked and copied between machines without any byte changing. The data is cut into small pieces. Each piece is fingerprinted, and the pieces are arranged in a tree. Repeated content is stored once. Any byte range can be read back and checked on its own. When a file changes a little, only the changed pieces need to travel. It does not shrink new text; unique text takes about twice as much room. It exists so that a future model has something exact to quote from.
375.breadcrumbs: The mechanism board » Exact byte object store » In plain words
375.title: In plain words

376.body: Nothing. A transformer has no part like it. It sits beneath the model as durable memory outside it. The nearest transformer idea is a key-value cache that survives a restart, but this store holds raw source bytes with no keys, no facts and no addresses. Exact memory is the part that would address facts. Its node ids are content fingerprints and are never geometric addresses. A document drawn as a row of 32-byte tiles folding into a three-child tree with a root fingerprint on top. A highlighted 23-byte range lights only the branches that cover it: 8 verified nodes, 384 bytes. Beside it, two versions of a file with shared subtrees greyed out and only the changed records travelling. Below, a bar chart of stored sizes for four test files. Left, a small read touches only a few verified nodes. Middle, an edit sends only the changed records. Right, repeats shrink and unique text grows.

377.body: Cutting and folding (proof of the format, measurement of the sizes). fold(bytes) splits the data into ordered 32-byte atoms. The last atom is zero-padded. A 32,768-byte object is therefore 1,024 atoms. The atoms become the leaves of a canonical ternary (three-child) tree of records. A record holds a scale byte and a 12-byte fingerprint (BLAKE2b-96, a hash) of the scale and payload. After that comes either a 32-byte leaf or three ordered 12-byte child ids. A leaf record is 45 bytes and an internal record is 49. A child's scale must equal its parent's scale minus one, which forbids cycles. Equal chunks hash to the same record, so repeated content is stored once while every ordered occurrence is kept. Manifest and version. A manifest pins the length, the ordered roots and a whole-object SHA-256. The object version is the SHA-256 of the canonical manifest. rebuild checks the padding and the whole-object SHA-256, so the byte obligation is \[\mathrm{rebuild}(\mathrm{fold}(b)) = b\] for every input \(b\) within the limits (a tested obligation, with 20 integration controls at delivery; not a machine-checked proof). Range reads. range(start..end) descends only the branches that intersect the range. It authenticates each visited record against the root. A 23-byte read of a 32,768-byte object touched 2 leaves and needed 8 authenticated nodes, 384 serialized bytes. A missing, unrelated leaf did not block that range. It did block a full rebuild. Token bindings. Occurrence bindings tie every token occurrence of a pinned tokenizer to an object version and a byte span. They are versioned separately from the object, so exact token, occurrence and version identity never merges with a geometric address. The adapter refuses lossy or normalised sources instead of guessing offsets. Peers. A receiver asks only for node ids it is missing, verifies each digest, and commits all at once or not at all. The wire format is specified byte by byte in PROTOCOL.md . What it does not do. Deduplication is not general compression. Unique 32,768-byte content takes 70,972 record bytes, which is \(70{,}972/32{,}768\approx 2.17\) times the raw size (measurement). Pins prove integrity, not who sent the data. No collision fixture was built for the 12-byte node id. Rule check. There is no model, no learning and no geometry here. The source has no softmax, sigmoid or tanh (searched), no matrix multiplication and no floating point apart from a test timer. The hash primitives are integer. No instruction-level audit against the zero-multiplier serving rule (D11) has been run. It adds nothing to the discrete training path (D32).

385.body: Ask a model "Ana's locker is 47. Ben's locker is 12. What is Ana's locker?" A common failure is to find a stated number but pick the wrong one. During training, a teacher marks which earlier words hold the value the question asks for, and which hold the other stated values. The model is rewarded when its attention lands on the right ones. Nothing changes when the model is used: the labels only shape what the attention learns. It aims at one failure, "found a value, but the wrong one".

386.body: It adds to the loss, the training score. A transformer is usually trained only to predict the next word, and nothing tells its attention which earlier word to look at. This adds a second target on the attention read itself. It replaces no layer and adds no operation at serving time. Attention bars over the passage about Ana's and Ben's lockers. Before training the attention is split between 47 and 12, with bound mass 0.73 and competing mass 0.14. After training it piles onto 47, at 0.90. Beside it, a paired comparison of wrong-value counts over 120 memory rows, and a bar chart of the memory score when each read layer is silenced in turn. Left, attention before and after supervision. Right, the wrong-value count falls, and silencing the supervised layer removes the answers.
386.breadcrumbs: The mechanism board » Read binding » What it replaces in a transformer
386.title: What it replaces in a transformer

387.body: For a question whose next word belongs to a stated value, the training data carries two sets of earlier positions. \(B\) is the set that holds the asked value (bound). \(C\) is the set that holds the other stated values (competing). The labels come from a sidecar file written with the dialogue corpus. Each attention head \(h\) puts weight \(a^{(h)}_j\) on earlier position \(j\). Define the bound and competing mass: \[m^{(h)}_{\text{bound}}=\sum_{j\in B}a^{(h)}_j,\qquad m^{(h)}_{\text{comp}}=\sum_{j\in C}a^{(h)}_j .\] The extra loss, on the best-binding head, is \[\mathcal{L}_{\text{bind}}=-\log\!\Big(\max_h m^{(h)}_{\text{bound}}+10^{-6}\Big),\qquad \mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{\text{language}}+W\,\mathcal{L}_{\text{bind}} .\] The floor \(10^{-6}\) keeps the logarithm finite. The weight \(W\) was 0.1 in the run kept and 0.5 in the first test. The loss is zero only when all attention sits on the bound positions (ignoring the floor). That follows from the formula (proof). One variant also penalised competing mass with \(0.5\,\max(0,\,m_{\text{comp}}-0.03)\). The labels never touch a hidden state or a score for the next word. The served network is unchanged, and only the read learns to separate values. The tested runs applied it to a late read layer (layer 8, in a stack whose reads are layers 2, 5 and 8) from step 0 of a fine-tune. An exact-by-construction variant (read_lineage = phase_bind) gives each value a fixed phase tag, so binding is exact rather than learned. A random rotation tag is its control. Rule check. Rule Verdict No softmax (D23) Broken in the tested form. The loss has no softmax, but the mass \(m\) comes from a softmax attention read ( attention-state review : "it is a softmax read") No matrix multiplication (D30) Not clean. The 29M-parameter stack that was trained is a dense matrix-multiplication stack Integer-only serving (D11) Nothing to serve. It is a training signal and adds no served operation Discrete path (D32) and offline float (D37) Not on the discrete path. Float training is legal offline under D37 , so the signal is admissible if attached to a lawful read and exported to an integer artifact

397.body: The copy mixture. The model's next-word distribution blends its ordinary scores with a copy distribution: \[p(v)=(1-g)\,\mathrm{softmax}(z)_v+g\sum_{j:\,x_j=v}a_j ,\] where \(g\) is a learned gate, \(x_j\) is the word at earlier position \(j\), and \(a_j\) is the pointer's attention over a window of earlier words. The first term uses a softmax, which matters for the rule check below. The project-specific part is how a source is chosen. Every word has a registered prime. A source \(j\) is admitted when the greatest common divisor of its atoms and the query's atoms exceeds 1: \[\gcd(q,\pi_j)>1 ,\] or when an ordered n-let (a short ordered run of atoms) matches. These are RouteAdmission::SharedAtom and Ngram. Rarer atoms weigh more, by \(\ln\gcd\). The route score is scaled by 4.0 (ROUTE_SHARPNESS), and the attention is a softmax over admitted sources. An identity term (PointerIdentity) adds the overlap of the six words before the source with the six before the query. A fixed table folds upper and lower case and one leading space to a canonical id ( copy_identity.rs ). It only decides matches and never changes the emitted word. The intended key is the slot address: entity prime times attribute prime, written when the fact is stated. Not the wording around the value. That version was never built. Rule check. Rule Verdict No softmax (D23) Broken as built. Both the mixture and the pointer attention use softmax. The form is a softmax pointer and could not be served (project history, era 28) No matrix multiplication (D30) Not clean. The pointer sits inside a dense float model and its score is a dot product Integer-only serving (D11) Export serves only an unrouted, unselected pointer. A pointer with an identity term is refused at export. The fold table is one table read plus integer equality Discrete path (D32) and offline float (D37) No pointer exists on the discrete path. D37 would allow an offline float re-registration in a separately scanned module, with an integer export and a reported gap. Nothing is released

405.body: Instead of running a full feed-forward layer, the model reads a handful of rows from a very large table. The row addresses come from the 240 special points of the E8 lattice, an eight-dimensional pattern of points (the E8 roots). A fast exact rule finds the nearest special point to each half of the query. The hope is a fixed, exact address book that touches a few rows per token rather than running a full dense layer. In the one trial, the fixed address book did slightly worse than an address book the model learns for itself.

406.body: The feed-forward block (also called the MLP). In a transformer this is the large layer after attention that processes each word, and it holds most of the arithmetic. Here a table lookup of a few rows takes its place. The table is far larger, but only a few rows are read per token. The 240 E8 roots drawn as a ring of 15 coloured clusters of 16. A query half snaps to its nearest root and the other 15 members of that root's orbit light up as candidates. Beside it, a 240 by 240 grid of value slots where two selections cross and the top 8 cells light up, next to a dense layer drawn as a full block. Below, a four-bar chart of held-out bits per byte with the 0.0054 noise band marked. Left, how a query picks candidate rows. 407.body: The E8 roots (the count is proof; the integer decode was checked by measurement on 20,000 queries). The 240 roots are 112 vectors of the form \((\pm1,\pm1,0,0,0,0,0,0)\) in any arrangement, plus 128 vectors \((\pm\tfrac12,\dots,\pm\tfrac12)\) with an even number of minus signs. The code stores them in doubled integer coordinates, so they are exact integers. Per head, in four steps. Cut and decode. The query is cut into two 8-dimensional halves. Each half is decoded to its nearest E8 root in \(O(8)\) operations: the two largest \(|x_i|\) with sign rules, or all signs with a parity fix for the half-integer roots. No 240-way scan is needed. It was checked against a full scan on 20,000 queries. Orbits. SpiralCore's group of 64 signed axis permutations (\(\mathrm{Cl}(0,6)\)) splits the 240 roots into 15 orbits of 16 (240 = 15 × 16). A half's candidates are the 16 roots of its decoded root's orbit. Slots. The two halves together address a grid of \(240\times240=57{,}600\) value slots. The head keeps the top \(k\) by combined score (\(k=8\) in the rung that ran). Read. A kept slot of rank \(r\) is weighted by \[w_r = R[h][r]\cdot\sigma(\beta s+\gamma),\] a learned rank table \(R\) times a logistic-sigmoid gate on the score \(s\). There is no softmax. The output is the weighted sum of the kept value rows. Slot choice is detached from training, so only the query map, rank table, gate scale and the values learn. Size. The value table has \(57{,}600\times256\) float values, about 59 MB per layer (proof by arithmetic: \(57{,}600\times256\times4\) bytes). A token reads 32 of its rows. The design arithmetic is about 27 thousand multiply-adds per token against 270 thousand for the dense layer it replaces, roughly tenfold. That figure is arithmetic, not a measured speed or energy saving. Rule check. Rule Verdict No softmax (D23) Broken as built. The read weight uses a sigmoid, and sigmoid is banned along with softmax No matrix multiplication (D30) Not clean. The query map and value mixing are dense float operations. The static E8 and SpiralCore tables were rebuilt without a generic 8 by 8 matrix product ( record ) Integer-only serving (D11) No served form. Export refuses, and integer serving refuses product-key memory. The value tables are float. The decode, orbit tables and route transport are exact integer lookups Discrete path (D32) and offline float (D37) Not on the discrete path. D37 would allow offline float training only as a new reviewed sheet with an integer export and a reported gap

416.body: A normal network stores each weight as a decimal number, and using it costs a multiplication. Here each weight is only −1, 0 or +1, so using it means add, subtract or skip. Two bit patterns are compared by counting how many bits differ, which is called the Hamming distance. The hope was cheap arithmetic with no multiplier. The plan to replace the big grids of multiplications this way has not been adopted, because every weight is still touched for every word and the owner's no-dense-matrix-multiplication rule counts that against it. The bit counting and the three-way switches are used in the current model.
416.breadcrumbs: The mechanism board » Ternary and XOR/Hamming arithmetic » In plain words
416.title: In plain words

417.body: The arithmetic inside the big grids of multiplications (the matrix multiplications): the projections that turn each word's vector into queries, values and layer outputs. Three panels. Left: a row of 16 ternary weights stored as two bit strips, one marking +1 and one marking -1, and an activation bit strip. An AND mask lights the surviving bits, and the two bit counts are subtracted. Middle: two 8-coordinate E8 root vectors drawn as bar rows with differing coordinates highlighted, where a tie in L1 displacement is broken by the Hamming count. Right: a dense grid with every weight cell lit beside a routed grid with only a few cells lit. The operators are AND and subtract, not XOR (left). Inside the current model, bit counting breaks ties between routes (middle). The multiplier goes away but the dense grid stays (right).
417.breadcrumbs: The mechanism board » Ternary and XOR/Hamming arithmetic » What it replaces in a transformer
417.title: What it replaces in a transformer

418.body: Storage (Definition). A ternary weight vector \(w\in\{-1,0,+1\}^n\) is stored in two bit planes. Plane \(P\) is set where \(w_i=+1\), plane \(N\) where \(w_i=-1\), and \(P\wedge N=0\). The repository's low-bit code uses two bits per weight (CODE_POS=1, CODE_NEG=2), which is the same thing. The dot product is exact (proof). For a binary activation vector \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), \[\sum_i w_i x_i \;=\; \operatorname{popcount}(P\wedge x)-\operatorname{popcount}(N\wedge x).\] Each position contributes \(+1\) if and only if \(P_i=x_i=1\), and \(-1\) if and only if \(N_i=x_i=1\). A zero weight is skipped for free. For multi-bit activations \(x=\sum_b 2^b x^{(b)}\), repeat per bit plane and combine with shifts and adds. A power-of-two row scale is a shift. A 2026-10-12 re-check agreed in 5,000 random trials ( measurement , owner-ruling record ). XOR is not the ternary dot product (proof). XOR gives the Hamming distance \(d(a,b)=\operatorname{popcount}(a\oplus b)=|a|+|b|-2|a\wedge b|\). Over the two-element field GF(2), \(-1\) and \(+1\) are the same element, so "ternary XOR matmul" is false as stated. What is true is the AND-and-subtract identity above. What it does not remove (proof, by counting). A layer with \(D\) inputs and \(W\) outputs still reads all \(W\times D\) weights for every token. The multiplier disappears; the dense sum stays. A contraction applied only to a routed subset would not have this cost ( hypothesis ). Where it runs today (Definition). In the discrete model the same ingredients serve as routing parts, in discrete.cu : A coordinate Hamming count breaks ties when two candidate ports have equal L1 displacement for a transported query. A ternary gate parameter switches flock levels on or off, with candidates visited in the order 0, −1, +1. Geometry. On its own this is Boolean hypercube arithmetic, not a lattice. The E8 lattice is the (8,4,4) Hamming code lifted by Construction A, but Hamming distance on E8 labels is not the E8 lattice distance (decision D32). Rule check. D11 (integer serving): compatible in form, since add, subtract, skip and AND with popcount need no multiplier. Not shown to be fast: the one multiplier-free engine measured ran 68.0 tokens/s against 127.5 on the D10 engine (multiplies allowed) ( record ). D23 (no softmax): nothing to scan; scoring is a hard count. D25/D30 (no dense matrix multiplication): the dense ternary sum is still a dense sum, so it would not pass as a matmul substitute. The tie-break and trit gates inside routing are not matmuls. D32/D37: D32 names ternary and Hamming computation as a preferred substrate. D37 allows float training offline, but a ternary master would still need a new pre-registered sheet and an export gap ( decisions ).

427.body: A network's weight matrix is usually a grid of independent numbers. Here each 4-by-4 block of the grid is replaced by one quaternion, a set of four numbers that describes a turn and a scale in four dimensions. That makes the grid four times smaller. After training, each quaternion is rounded to one of 120 exact rotations of the icosahedron (the 20-sided solid), plus a small scale. A product of two such rounded blocks then becomes a table lookup and a few shifts and adds, with no multiplication. The size and quality results were good. The speed benefit was never built or measured.

429.body: Compact form (Definition). Each projection map is stored as an array \(Q[\text{out}/4,\ \text{in}/4,\ 4]\), one quaternion \((a,b,c,d)\) per 4×4 block, so there are four times fewer weights. A block acts as the Hamilton left-multiplication matrix \[L(a,b,c,d)=\begin{pmatrix}a&-b&-c&-d\\ b&a&-d&c\\ c&d&a&-b\\ d&-c&b&a\end{pmatrix}.\] The output quaternion is \(y_j=\sum_k Q_{jk}\otimes x_k\), with the input read as \(\text{in}/4\) quaternions. Each block costs 16 multiply-adds, so by itself the compact form saves weights, not arithmetic ( measurement : width 256 uses the same 5,537,792 multiply-adds per token as the dense width-256 model). Snap (Definition). Each trained quaternion becomes \[m\cdot 2^{e}\cdot\Big(g_1+\tfrac14\,g_2\Big),\] where \(g_1\) is the nearest of the 120 unit icosians (the binary icosahedral group, exact over \(\mathbb Z[\varphi]\)), \(g_2\) is the icosian nearest the leftover residual, \(m\in\{1,\,1.25,\,1.5,\,1.75\}\) is a 2-bit mantissa and \(e\) is a power of two. That is about 19 to 20 bits per block instead of 128 for four 32-bit floats. Activations can be snapped to the same set after training. Table product (Definition, never built). The 120 icosians multiply by a fixed 120×120 table. The records describe a snapped product as a table read plus shifts and at most two adds. The group table itself was verified: all 14,400 products (120×120) matched in the 2026-09-20 prefix-recovery check ( measurement , record ). A kernel that serves exact-set by exact-set block products was never written. Why one icosian is too coarse (measurement). The 120 directions sit about 15 degrees apart. Adding the residual icosian cut the mean angle error from 14.75 to 4.73 degrees, about 9 times less direction error energy. Rule check. D11 (integer serving): the weight side is multiplier-free by design. The activation side and the table kernel were never built, and export of quaternion-weight models is refused in the code. D23 (no softmax): the mechanism has none; snaps pick the nearest point. D25/D30 (no dense matrix multiplication): fails as run. The forward expanded each map to a dense matrix and called a library matrix multiply, and the snap itself was a matmul against the 120 icosians. The fused Hamilton kernel (OP2) is a handwritten dense block contraction, which D25 does not accept as a replacement. Both execution paths now refuse. The ban retired the contraction; it was not retired by a negative result. D32/D37: the historical form is float. D32 froze it and D37 lets it back only as a new offline float sheet with a fresh review ( decisions ).

438.body: Inside a feed-forward layer, a gate decides how much of a signal passes through. The usual gate squashes a number into the range 0 to 1 with a sigmoid curve, and the project's rules now ban that curve. This gate instead turns a gate signal into a rotation in four dimensions and rotates the matching value by it, four numbers at a time. A rotation only turns a vector. It uses no exponential and no squashing. A consequence worth knowing: a rotation cannot make a vector shorter, so this gate steers the signal rather than switching it off. Whether that is enough is not yet known.

440.body: Work on blocks of four numbers. Let \(g\) be a gate block and \(u\) the matching "up" (value) block of the hidden layer. Compute \[r=\sqrt{|g|^2+10^{-12}},\qquad q=g/r,\qquad \text{out}=q\otimes u,\] where \(\otimes\) is the Hamilton product (the quaternion product) and \(q\otimes u=L(q)\,u\) with the \(4\times4\) matrix \(L\) given on the spin-weights page . Two facts (proof). Quaternion length is multiplicative, \(|q\otimes u|=|q|\,|u|\), and \(|q|=|g|/\sqrt{|g|^2+10^{-12}}\). So \(|{\rm out}|=|u|\) up to a factor that falls below 1 only when \(|g|\) is near \(10^{-6}\) or smaller (at \(|g|=10^{-6}\) the factor is \(0.71\)). A zero gate block gives \(q=0\) and zero output. The output's length is set by \(u\) alone; the gate sets only its direction. The backward pass is exact, including the normalisation ( Definition ): \[\partial u=\bar q\otimes d,\qquad \partial q=d\otimes\bar u,\qquad \partial g=\frac{\partial q-q\,(q\cdot\partial q)}{r},\] with \(d\) the incoming adjoint and \(\bar q\) the quaternion conjugate. No exp, sigmoid, tanh or softmax appears in either direction. The hazard (proof, from the formula). Because \(\partial g\) divides by \(r\), a gate block near zero gives a gradient of about \(1/r\approx10^{6}\). Weight decay can push a block toward zero. No real run has checked this. Wiring. The hidden width must be divisible by 4. One GPU thread handles one block. The setting gate=hamilton selects it; the default stays the sigmoid SwiGLU gate so old artifacts load byte for byte. Export for integer serving and quantisation-aware training refuse any non-default gate. The same operation is also the output gate of the geometric recurrence . What the owner's card left open (hypothesis). An icosian snap of \(q\), so the product becomes a read in the 120×120 table; an exact hard forward with a straight-through gradient bridge; and a serving form. Rule check. D11 (integer serving): not servable today. The exporter refuses other gates, and the normalisation divides by a square root and multiplies two runtime values. It becomes table-servable only after the icosian snap makes \(q\) one of 120 rotations. D23 (no softmax or squashing): passes by construction. D25 closed the sigmoid exception that SwiGLU relied on, which this replaces. D25/D30 (no dense matrix multiplication): a per-block Hamilton product is not a dense contraction. The owner permits a geometric feed-forward block of this gate plus Hamilton-block projections, and the projection half has since been replaced by SpiralCore/FBS . D32/D37: a float operation, frozen by D32. D37 lets it return only through a new pre-registered offline sheet ( decisions ).

448.body: A recurrent layer keeps a running memory and decides at each step how fast old content fades and how much new input gets in. The old recipe used smooth curves for those decisions (sigmoid, exponential, tanh), and the project's rules now ban them. The replacement opens the input with a clamped straight line, picks the fade rate from a short table of powers of two, and carries the memory forward by a rotation. Each step is a table read and a rotation, so nothing smooth is needed. It is a drop-in for the gates of one particular recurrent design, not a standard part of a transformer.

449.body: A plain transformer has no recurrence, so this replaces nothing there directly. It belongs to the recurrent alternative to attention used in the project's older float stack. In that design it replaces four squashing functions inside the recurrence: a sigmoid opening, an exponential and softplus decay rate, and a tanh-shaped output gate. Left: a staircase of the 16 fade rates 2 to the minus s plus 1 against the opening score from 0 to 1, laid over the smooth curve it replaces; the selected step and its two neighbours, which the credit rule compares, are marked. Middle: quaternion lanes drawn as arrows that rotate and shrink each step by the chosen rate, with the fade rate and the keep factor shown as two sides of a right triangle inscribed in a unit circle. Right: retention of one remembered token over 32 steps for several table rates, each a clean power of two, beside the historical continuous curve. A table of 16 fixed clocks replaces a smooth dial. Each step multiplies the old state by the chosen rate and a rotation, and adds new input scaled by the matching keep factor.

450.body: The trunk's sequence mixer is a recurrence over lanes of four numbers (quaternions). From the source ( geometric_stack.rs ), one step per lane is \[h_t \;=\; \lambda_t\,u_t\otimes h_{t-1}\;+\;\kappa_t\,b_t,\] where \(u_t\) is a unit quaternion built from the gate projections (the rotation), \(b_t\) is the convolved input drive, and \(\otimes\) is the quaternion product. Four squashing sites of the historical form are replaced in the mode rec_gates=geometric: Opening (Definition). \(s_t=\mathrm{clamp}(g_t+d,\,0,\,1)\), where \(g_t\) is the gate projection and \(d\) is a per-lane decay parameter read raw, with no softplus. The clamp has an exact subgradient. Rate (Definition). The index is \(i=\min(\lfloor 16\,s_t\rfloor,\,15)\). The rate and the keep factor are read from two 16-entry tables: \[\lambda=2^{-(i+1)},\qquad \kappa=\sqrt{1-\lambda^2}.\] The rates are exact powers of two, from \(1/2\) down to \(2^{-16}\), and \(\kappa\) is precomputed beside each one, so serving needs only table reads. The pair \((\lambda,\kappa)\) lies on the unit circle up to \(6\times10^{-8}\) ( measurement ; the last four \(\kappa\) entries round to exactly 1 in 32-bit floats). Carry (unchanged). The quaternion scan above. Output gate (Definition). The Hamilton rotation gate on the recurrence output, replacing a tanh-shaped gate. Credit through a hard choice (Definition). Picking a table entry has zero derivative almost everywhere, so nothing would train. The backward pass uses a declared secant surrogate : it pairs the incoming adjoints for \((\lambda,\kappa)\) with the full counterfactual change in the table between the selected entry and each neighbour, and resolves the contrast along the fixed edge of length \(1/16\), half to each side and the whole weight to the single neighbour at either end. No probability or exponential is involved. It is a rule, not the derivative of hard selection, and whether it yields descent is the open test. A reading of the source (proof from the table, not a recorded finding). Every table entry satisfies \(\lambda\le\tfrac12\), so a step keeps at most half of the old state times a rotation. The historical rate \(\lambda=\exp(8\,\sigma(g)\log\sigma(d))\) can approach 1 as the opening goes to 0. Whether a table capped at one half per step keeps enough long memory is untested. The mode refuses non-GPU devices, export and quantisation-aware training. The historical mode stays the default so old artifacts reproduce. Rule check. D11 (integer serving): designed for it, since the rates are table reads, the opening is a clamp and the scan is rotations. Not yet exportable, because the integer engine binds the historical decay parameter. The output gate still needs the icosian snap. D23 (no softmax or squashing): a grep on 13 October found 0 squash-family tokens in the geometric arms (the historical branches keep 8 by design). D25/D30 (no dense matrix multiplication): a clamp, a table read, a scan and a per-block rotation. The no-matmul and no-softmax counters were unchanged by the delivering PR. D32/D37: a float operator. D32 froze it and D37 allows it back only by a new offline sheet ( decisions ). The active discrete model carries no recurrent state, so this belongs to a separate float trunk.

458.body: A normal layer mixes every input into every output using learned weights. This one does something much simpler. Each output block picks one input block from a small tree of stored blocks, three branches per node, and moves it along a path of exact steps in an eight-dimensional lattice called E8. Each step only swaps coordinates and flips signs. No learned coefficient is multiplied in; the path itself does the transforming. The trade is that each output reads one input block instead of a blend of all of them, and nobody has yet measured whether that carries enough information.

46.body: The owner's reason is cost, not taste: "to ban expensive operations" ( charter , section 1). Softmax turns scores into probabilities with exponentials and a sum over everything, and it hides a dense global normalisation. The charter bans it, and every softmax-like function, in the model, its training, its comparators and any renamed or table form (section 3.2). The price is real: every earlier read that learned a ranking had softmax helping it somewhere in training, and the best softmax-free read was a recorded REJECT, 0.0172 bits per byte worse and 15% slower ( measurement , open questions , record ). Whether a softmax-free read can learn ranking at all is the project's biggest open question.

460.body: The tree (Definition). Input channels are 8-dimensional integer atoms kept by a static Rust compiler in ordered base-3 binders. The compiler stores children, parent links, atom identity, support length and the incomplete frontier (at most 6,560 atoms, 16 frontier roots and 8 stages). FBS is the project's name for this tree. Exact atom identity stays separate from the geometric state. The steps (Definition, from SpiralCore). SpiralCore is an external exact-geometry source (a hosted file, reviewed on 9 October). Octonion left actions give 15 generators \(B\), each a signed coordinate permutation of \(\mathbb R^8\) with \(B^2=-I\). They act on the 16 roots of one E8 anchor orbit through 64 signed operator states. A breadth-first search over these labelled edges gives an ordered history between any two roots, composed by left-composition. Exact inverse (proof). From \(B^2=-I\) it follows \(B^4=I\) and so \(B^3=B^{-1}\). The inverse of a history is therefore the reversed sequence with each step cubed. Forward pass (Definition). The model stores query points \(z\in\mathbb R^{[\text{output blocks},\ \text{stages},\ 8]}\). At each stage a query picks the nearest root of the fixed orbit, and the history between roots composes a signed action \(A_j\). Output block \(j\) selects one atom \(\sigma(j)\) and transports it: \[y_j \;=\; A_j\,x_{\sigma(j)} .\] The forward is a gather and a sign. The input adjoint is the exact inverse action, \(A_j^{-1}\delta_j\), scattered to the selected atom. No coefficient exists for any input-output pair (proof, by construction). Credit for the query (Definition). Selecting a root is a hard choice. The query credit is a declared secant surrogate on root edges: force each lawful sibling, reroute its descendants, pair the output credit with the displacement of the carried block, and resolve along the edge. It is not the derivative of hard selection. The capacity question (proof of the count, hypothesis of the consequence). Each output block reads exactly one input atom, so an output block has one connection where a dense projection has all of them. Whether one transported atom per block is enough, or whether a small routed set per block is needed, has not been compared. The path runs on the GPU only; the CPU fallback is refused. Rule check. D11 (integer serving): the float form (32-bit and half-precision) is not servable. Sign flips, permutations and table reads need no multiplier, and the integer descendant in crates/uor-r4-discrete is integer-only on the GPU. D23 (no softmax): no probability weights, no normalised exponentials and no learned input-output coefficient grids; selection is hard by distance. The no-softmax counter was 1649 of 1649 on the delivering PR. D25/D30 (no dense matrix multiplication): retires the dense Hamilton contraction. The no-matmul counter fell from 95 to 93. Static table construction reads no model tensors and is not model compute. D32/D37: the float form was frozen by D32 and can return only by re-registration under D37. The integer transport is the substrate D32 names as the backbone, and it is the ACTIVE model path ( decisions ).

468.body: This was the project's main trained language model from late September to mid-October 2026, between 7 and 214 million parameters. It reads text through a stack of layers. Most layers carry a running memory made of four numbers, a "spinner" called a quaternion. At every word the spinner is turned a little and the old memory fades. A few layers look back over earlier words, and every layer ends in a small feed-forward block. It was trained on GPUs, then rounded to whole numbers so a laptop could run it. It produced chat-style replies, though only 43 of 232 reply checks passed and it was served through the integer engine on pod CPUs. It used arithmetic the project later banned, and it never reached its quality bars.

471.body: Layer pattern (definition). Layers repeat in a pattern such as rrarra. Each r is a recurrence layer and each a a read layer. Every layer is followed by a feed-forward block, inside a residual stream with RMS normalisation. Recurrence (definition). Lanes of four channels hold a quaternion state \(h_t\). Per token, \[h_t = \lambda_t\,(u_t \otimes h_{t-1}) + \sqrt{1-\lambda_t^{2}}\;c_t ,\] where \(\otimes\) is the Hamilton product, \(u_t\) is a unit quaternion computed from the input (it starts at the identity), \(\lambda_t\) is a gated decay with timescales spread from 2 to about 1,000 tokens, and \(c_t\) is a width-4 causal convolution of the input. Multiplying by a unit quaternion is a rotation of 4-space, so \(u_t\) turns the memory without changing its length. Reads and feed-forward. Read layers attend over earlier positions with a dot-product, Euclidean or Lorentz hyperbolic-distance score. Feed-forward blocks are SwiGLU with dense projections. Optional parts were a copy-pointer head, a product-key memory that replaced a feed-forward block or the last read, and flock or starling rank reads. Training and serving. Trained in float on GPU at 7M, 19.9M, 29M and 214M parameters, then exported to 4-bit grouped weights and served by the integer engine described in lut-serving . Where the arithmetic went (measurement, an operation count of the deployed 29M stack, width 576, 10 layers). Of 30,270,720 multiply-adds per token, the feed-forward blocks took 39.6 percent, recurrence projections 31.0 percent, reads 16.6 percent (40.5 percent at 4,096 tokens of context) and the output head 7.4 percent. The quaternion rotations took 16,128 multiplies, or 0.05 percent. The prime addresses, zeta phases and exact store took none, because they were not in the trained base ( geometry audit ). Rule check. Rule Verdict for the trained form No softmax or squashing anywhere ( D23 ) Broken. Softmax reads, a sigmoid decay gate, a softplus-shaped decay rate, SiLU in the feed-forward block and a GELU output gate No matrix multiplication ( D30 ) Broken. Dense projections and feed-forward blocks are matrix products, and the old kernels used tensor cores Integer serving ( D11 ) Served bit-for-bit against its quantised reference, but every weight is read for every token (about 30.2 million parameters at 29M), which the sparsity rule calls non-compliant Offline float, with an export gap ( D37 ) Float training would be legal again only in a separately scanned module with lawful parts. Past export gaps: 0.00883 bits per byte on identical positions for the 19.9M stack, and +0.0257 nats with GPTQ on the 7M stack

479.body: This was the project's first approach, from June to August 2026. Let an ordinary language model, the "teacher", read a lot of text. Record what it prefers in each situation and store those preferences as huge lookup tables. To answer, a small program finds the matching table row and picks the best next word using only whole-number adds and comparisons, with no multiplying. On a held-out set of 72,130 positions its table choice agreed with the target word 29.52% of the time, against 28.12% for the earlier runtime. It never wrote coherent text on its own, and building the tables needs a transformer teacher, which the project now forbids. The file format and the run-time program are kept as a tested reference.

482.body: Offline (compile). A teacher transformer (SmolLM2 or GPT-2) runs over a corpus and its preferences are recorded. A compiler packs them into an R4G1 graph, a content-addressed file holding: records keyed by hashed context codes (recent-token n-grams and prefix regions); a cover of regions induced by entropy-gain splits; pre-rounded integer score tables for each region; optional extra lanes (skip-mix candidate injection, segment, trajectory); certificates comparing the graph with the teacher on held-out positions. Compilation, certification and every teacher run are offline and unrestricted. Online (run). To pick the next token the program: hashes the recent tokens into a context code; takes the exact-context record, or the best-matching region (nearest match over compact bit signatures by counting differing bits, scored with a shift-and-add dot product in place of a multiply); adds each evidence source's stored integer scores, each counted once, saturating at the limits; breaks ties by a fixed rule and emits the best token. In symbols (definition), with \(E\) the set of evidence sources found and \(r_e[t]\) the stored score of token \(t\) from source \(e\) in fixed-point arithmetic (\(v\) is stored as the integer nearest to \(v\cdot 2^{16}\)): \[S(t)=\operatorname{sat}\Big(\sum_{e\in E} r_e[t]\Big),\qquad \hat t=\arg\max_t S(t).\] The frozen kernel contract permits only XOR, AND, OR, shifts, rotates, bit counting, integer add and subtract, comparisons and table reads. There is no float, multiply, divide or allocation after setup ( inference contract ). Geometry tried inside this frame. Prime and zeta-phase routing keys, Hopf S3-to-S2 observation, E8 and 120-root codebooks, H4/icosian frames, max-plus route composition and Furey algebra modules. Only the E8 codebook (better than sign codes at matched bits) and the integer shift-and-add dot product kept measured value. The rest tied or lost, and the Furey modules were never wired into inference. Rule check. Rule Verdict Integer serving ( D11 ) The frozen kernel is D11's ancestor and is compliant as a kernel. No per-token parameter-access count was recorded, so the sparsity rule (D5-b) is unmeasured No softmax ( D23 ) Run-time scoring is softmax-free by contract. The offline path used the teacher's probabilities, and the retired compiler and runtime modules carry float and softmax content that may not be restored No matrix multiplication ( D30 ) The frozen runtime has none. Compiling needs a transformer forward pass, which is banned anywhere, and no transformer teacher or comparator is allowed (D28) Offline float ( D37 ) Float compiling would be legal in principle, but the teacher is separately banned. Nothing here is on the discrete GPU path, and the graph crates no longer build against the current core

490.body: This is how a finished model runs on an ordinary laptop or in a web browser using only whole numbers: adds, shifts and table look-ups. There is no decimal arithmetic and no multiply instruction. A trained model is exported to a compact file, mostly 4-bit numbers. A checker then reads the compiled program and counts machine instructions to prove that no multiply sneaks in. The engine reproduces its reference answers exactly, and the checks are green. But it has only served older models that fell short of their bars, and no model built under today's rules has been exported through it.

This changes how a model is computed, not what it is. The engine does not make a weak model better, and, as the history below shows, it still reads every stored weight for every token. Three panels. Left: one dot product done with table look-ups and a shift, with a counter reading zero multiplies. Middle: float and integer outputs on the diagonal, and a bar showing the real cost is weight rounding. Right: a strip of 44 native and 7 WebAssembly symbols, all counted zero multiply, divide and float instructions. Left, how a dot product needs no multiply. Middle, the engine is exact and the loss is in rounding the weights. Right, the audit counts instructions in the compiled program.

493.body: Export. Training is offline and may use float. For serving the weights go into a UORLUT01 container. Weights are 4-bit codes in groups of 32. Each group has a one-byte scale (a 4-bit mantissa and a 4-bit exponent). A few small integer tables cover the nonlinear steps (square root, decay rates, SiLU, arcosh, exp). One projection (definition). For a weight matrix \(W\) and an integer activation vector \(x\), the output is \(y_i=\sum_j w_{ij}x_j\), where each weight is a group scale times a 4-bit code, \(w_{ij}=s_g\,q_{ij}\) with \(s_g=m\,2^{e}\). The engine does not multiply \(q_{ij}\) by \(x_j\). For each activation it builds a 16-entry table \(T_j[q]=q\,x_j\), which needs only additions to fill, and then reads \(T_j[q_{ij}]\) for each weight. Four output rows are blocked to reuse the table. The scale \(s_g\) is applied by shifts and adds. Products of two runtime values. A score, a gate or a value mix needs a true product of two numbers known only at run time. The engine builds a table of the sixteen multiples of one operand by repeated addition, reads it at each base-16 digit of the other operand, and sums the reads with shifts: \(ab=\sum_k 16^k\,T_a[d_k(b)]\), exact by the definition of base-16 digits (proof; stack_mul_u64 and stack_mul_u128 in kernels.rs). The quarter-square identity would also be allowed, but the serving engine does not use it. Normalisation uses an integer square root or a table. Sampling is integer min-p. Session state. A conversation's state is saved and restored byte-for-byte (the UR4SESS1 format). The five rules (D11). R1: no floating point and no maths library. R2: no multiply or divide instruction. R3: dense per-token access to a learned store is interim, not the end state (D5). R4: no transformer backbone. R5: energy is claimed only when measured. The audit. The release binary is disassembled, and the multiply, divide and float instructions are counted over the serving symbols, natively and in WebAssembly. The audit proves absence of those instructions. It says nothing about model quality, and the SIMD kernels in the WebAssembly build are unintegrated fixtures that the 7-of-7 audit never exercises ( record ). Geometry, as exact finite tables. The 120-element icosian group's Cayley table (about 14 KiB), a 1,025-entry arcosh table for Lorentz read scores, icosian-pair weights and the Q30 Hopf observation are stored as tables. The current integer crate selects typed H4 geometry and checked integer arithmetic for the discrete model's own export ( native_geometry.rs ). Rule check. Rule Verdict Integer serving ( D11 ) This is D11. Exact against its quantised reference on every windowed check, with zero multiply, divide and float instructions on the audited symbols. The gap: about 30.2 million parameters are read per token for the 29M stack, which the sparsity rule ( D5-b ) calls non-compliant. Cache residency (D5-a) is unmeasured until hardware counters exist No softmax ( D23 ) Partly non-compliant today. Schemas 1 and 2 serve softmax attention through exp-table masses. Schema 3 serves a softmax-free flock rank read, but the trained arms missed the bar No matrix multiplication ( D30 ) Table-read matrix-vector products stream every weight each token, which D5 calls a dense multiply in disguise. The allowed target is selected addressed reads and exact geometry tables Offline float, with an export gap ( D37 ) Float training is legal offline. Every candidate must report its export gap on the same evaluator. No discrete-path export exists yet

50.body: The owner's rule is "use geometry", because the bet is that exact geometry can replace dense arithmetic ( charter , section 1). What has been shown is narrow. An injective code is possible by counting (\(16^4 = 65{,}536 \ge 4{,}096\), proof ), and the PrimeZeta construction gives all 4,096 tokens distinct vectors ( measurement ). 501.body: This is a small language model written from scratch in Rust. It treats every word as an exact prime-number address and keeps its memory as rotations in four-dimensional geometry. 504.body: Addresses and phases (definition). Each token has a full prime address, and ordered two-prime keys name contexts. Eight fixed zeta-zero phase channels, compiled to 16-bit turns, supply position-like phases. Window fold (definition). A window of recent tokens is folded, in order, into exact H4 coordinates. H4 is the 4-dimensional symmetry of the 600-cell, whose 120 corners are the unit icosians. Sums are exact pairs \(a+b\varphi\) with \(\varphi^2=\varphi+1\). Products stay exact because \[(a+b\varphi)(c+d\varphi)=(ac+bd)+(ad+bc+bd)\,\varphi \qquad\text{(proof, by } \varphi^2=\varphi+1).\] The fold keeps signed chirality and evicts old entries with a bound. Readout. Conditional score tables plus seven gated feature groups, with coefficients rounded to eighths and bounded shift-and-add arithmetic, predict the next piece. Selectors on top. Small learned tables, each fitted on constructed families, choose: which source occurrence to read; whether to write an exact owner-value relation (sixteen versions kept); whether to Copy, Add or Stop on typed numeric literals; how deep to read; and which version intent (initial, previous or current) to follow along a validated chain, abstaining when the chain is truncated. A shared geometric writer emits the answer. Exact occurrence and version identity stay separate from the geometric addresses, and digests are never used as meaning. October cross-state form. Trained 4-bit ("Q4") coefficients over categorical H4 banks (Context, Prefix, Generate), scored with exact integers. The training goal was a pooled-token ranking: for each token, push the correct answer above its strongest wrong rival, using \[\ell=\operatorname{softplus}\!\Big(\log\frac{m_{\text{rival}}}{m_{\text{gold}}}\Big),\] with \(m\) the score masses. That function is banned. The allowed replacement is the hinge \(\max(0,\ \delta-(s_{\text{gold}}-s_{\text{rival}}))\) of rank-margin . Training and serving. Training used floating point. Serving executes the rounded integer scores. The preserved source is excluded from the current build by cfg(any()) and the facade in native_support.rs. Rule check. Rule Verdict Integer serving ( D11 ) Partly. Scores are rounded integers with bounded shift-and-add, and an integer realizer ran with no source access (28 replies, 178 actions reproduced). Host tokenizing, fitting and reports use float, and no complete-binary instruction audit is recorded No softmax or squashing ( D23 ) Broken in the October line. The pooled loss uses softplus, log-sum-exp episode weights and softmax token weights. The September sampler used a float softmax No matrix multiplication ( D30 ) Unclear for September: its fitting was table search on the host. D29 quarantined the 14 native-context kernels and 1 selected-potential kernel after a hidden dense contraction was found Offline float, with an export gap ( D37 ) Float learning over Q4 coefficients would be legal once the objective is allowed and the module is separately scanned. The 4-bit grid builds in an export gap that was never reported against a float score

511.body: UOR-R4 is a research project, and for months it ran research the heavy way: one folder per pull request, a written plan before almost every step, and a review before each run. In the week of 12 to 18 October only 11% of the recorded lab work was a model result (see history ). Since 19 October 2026 the owner's charter keeps the rigour but drops the bulk. Each line of research has one notebook page with one row per result. A written plan is required only before a GPU run or a run that a milestone claim rests on. Old records are kept, untouched, in archive/. flowchart LR A["Question or idea"] --> B["Notebook page<br/>for its research line"] B --> C{"GPU training or<br/>evaluation, or a<br/>milestone claim?"} C -- no --> D["Build, test, run<br/>host checks"] C -- yes --> E["One-page sheet"] E --> F["Review by someone<br/>who is not the author"] F --> G["Owner releases<br/>the sheet once"] G --> H["Run on the GPU"] D --> I["New notebook row"] H --> I I --> J["Sealed artifacts and<br/>old records go to archive/"] The path of one piece of work. Only the right-hand branch needs a sheet, a review and an owner release. Terms follow the glossary . Claims are labelled proof , measurement or hypothesis as defined in formal_vocabulary.md . The rules below are the research clauses of the charter ; section numbers point there.
511.breadcrumbs: How research is done now » How research is done now
511.title: How research is done now

512.body: One notebook per research line (charter §5.6). A line is one sustained question, such as "how the discrete model reads context". Its notebook lives at docs/research/notebook/<line>.md. Each result is one row: date, what ran, the number, the bar it was tested against, the verdict and a link to the artifact. A dated evidence folder is kept only when a run seals artifacts. The one-page plan for the whole project is NOW.md ; with the notebooks, it replaces the old running log (current-state.md). A sheet only where it decides spend (§4.5). A sheet is a pre-registration of one page: the bar, the noise, the controls, the seeds, the cost and what each outcome would decide. It needs a review by a non-author, called a FIT review, before: any GPU training or evaluation, and any run that a milestone claim rests on. A fresh-context subagent counts as a non-author. Builds, finite kernel tests and host checks need no sheet. Old float sheets come back only as new sheets with a new FIT. A FIT review releases nothing by itself. One owner release per sheet (§5.1). The owner types one release phrase personally for each sheet. It covers all the sheet's arms, seeds and registered stop rules. Labs stage the commands and then check the records; no lab types a release for the owner. Mechanism statuses (§4.1). Every mechanism is ACTIVE (on the model path), READY (built and tested but not yet trained in) or PARKED (the tested forms failed or broke a rule). A PARKED page lists what would reopen it. There is no terminal status. The mechanism board shows the current state. This is the rule from decision D22 (a negative closes a configuration, never a mechanism). What a verdict closes. A negative result closes the exact tested configuration: the recipe, dose, window, key and objective. It never closes the mechanism, and stopping a novel mechanism takes an owner decision. A run that meets its own pre-registered mechanism target without a significant headline loss is a KEEP, and the work iterates. A tooling or numerical failure is a blocker to fix, not a negative. Source: D22 sections 1 and 2 in archive/integration/DECISIONS-2026-10-19.md . Instrument first (§4.2). Before calling a result, decide whether the check itself is faulty. An instrument defect is a fix, never a negative. No target is set from a vacuous instrument, and no single number rules out a line. Findings shows why: a metric that read zero, a control that checked zero rows and a typed-in number each misled the project once. Power and transfer (§4.3). A decisive run uses at least two seeds or at least 200 fresh rows. Its bar is never narrower than the measured noise. The mechanism must be trained in, not bolted on. Every gain on a development panel is reported together with a fresh transfer number. Controls and pivots (§4.4). Compare against lawful non-neural baselines, which today means count tables. After three results on one line that do not move its headline number, write a pivot note: stop, or run one decisive test. Plain verdict words. NOT_RUN means nothing ran; it is not a pass. UNAVAILABLE means a needed input was missing; it is not a negative. A passing test is not trained capability, and a passing control is not a language result (§4.6). Preserve everything (§4.7). Nothing is deleted. Negatives, unique source and other labs' work go to the archive, byte-identical.

516.body: The project's record holds more lessons about what misleads than results about what works. The most useful knowledge is a set of 21 lessons, mostly about how to measure honestly, plus a short list of measured results. The honest summary is this. Several lawful parts exist and have passed their finite tests. No model on the current path has learned language: the best trained discrete model sits below a simple count table. The cause is not yet established. flowchart TB A["Passes with the teacher's text supplied<br/>(teacher-forced)"] --> B["Passes on a panel the authors built"] B --> C["Passes on development rows<br/>the team has already seen"] C --> D["Passes on fresh held-out rows"] D --> E["Writes coherent text on its own"] E --> F["Same result from the shipped integer file"] F --> G["Faster or cheaper per token on a laptop"] The ladder a result must climb before it counts as capability. The project has repeatedly stopped at the first three steps (lessons 3 and 4 below).

519.body: Check the instrument before trusting a result. A metric that read 0.0000 hid a real loss (the #99 metric, removed by the revert #102 ). An outside check on the same text differed from the pipeline's own score by about a factor of three, 11.17 against 3.84 bits per token ( #300 ). Typed-in numbers were once merged as results ( #1459 ). A lookup-table gain was retracted as a constant shift ( #1881 ). A control that checked zero rows reported a pass ( #2112 ). Measure the shipped form. The trained model and the shipped artifact differed by 0.57 bits per byte (BPB) ( #1284 ). A teacher-forced or authored-panel pass is not coherent generation. Loss kept falling while prose stayed at 0 of 5 ( #948 , #1264 , #1398 ). Development is not fresh. A frozen-upstream adapter scored 437 of 512 on rows the team had seen, then 0 of 128 on a fresh draw ( #2162 , #2164 ). A gate set before a run does not move after a miss, and a missing input is not a negative. Frozen floors survived every re-entry ( #887 , #931 ). An UNAVAILABLE report is not a zero ( #661 , #986 ).
519.breadcrumbs: How research is done now » What the project knows » Check the measurement first
519.title: Check the measurement first

520.body: Fixed geometry usually tied or lost to a matched ordinary control. This held for W(3,3) ( #929 ), for the project's geometric mechanisms as of September ( #1371 ) and for fixed E8 or H4 codebooks against k-means ( #1456 ). Kept exceptions: quaternion transport ( #1460 ), quaternion and icosian weights ( #2193 , #2216 ) and seed reliability ( #1798 ). Some geometry wins were storage or lexical artifacts. A zeta-grid headline was storage banding ( #440 ); see also #487 . Exact algebra reproduces perfectly but carries no meaning on its own. H4 and the 64-state SpiralCore worked as controls and supplied no semantics ( #952 , #985 ). Shift-and-add stores and E8 codebooks beat sign codes at equal bits ( #243 , #395 ).

528.body: The project has built and tested many of the parts of a language model. The few it has trained together (the discrete writer, the reads and the ranking loss) have not yet beaten a simple count table, and a full trunk of lawful parts has never been trained. The biggest open question is simple to state: can a model that uses no softmax learn to rank the right word above the wrong ones? Nobody knows yet. Beside it sits a list of tests that were never run, or that failed only because the test was set up badly. Most of them are cheap, and the cheapest decisive one is FIT-reviewed and queued, not yet released. flowchart TD W2["W2: read-code capacity capture<br/>(FIT-reviewed, queued, about $0.91)"] --> Q{"Which wall is it?"} Q -- "representation (H_rep)" --> R["Fix the read and the address metric.<br/>Do not fund float training."] Q -- "learning law (H_law)" --> W3["W3: BVG-K batched discrete moves<br/>(about $12)"] W3 --> Q3{"Does integer top-1 beat<br/>both count tables?"} Q3 -- yes --> NX["Add the missing trunk slots,<br/>then export"] Q3 -- no --> W4["W4: one float-credit sheet<br/>(about $5 to $10 GPU)"] The order of the next decisive tests in the sequence the owner approved (D39 item 4); each is FIT-reviewed, none is released. W1, the K16 run, has already finished with no KEEP. Terms follow the glossary . Claims are labelled proof , measurement or hypothesis as in formal_vocabulary.md . Dollar figures are the chief architect's estimates, not recorded costs.

529.body: The model first picks a shortlist of candidate cells, the nearest K of 256 by address. A row counts as admitted if the right token survives that cut. It then ranks the shortlist and takes the nearest token. So a model can fail at admission, at ranking, or at both. 530.body: Can a softmax-free read learn ranking? This is a hypothesis, and the biggest one. Every float read that learned had softmax helping it somewhere in training. The best read without softmax, arm W, is a recorded REJECT. It was worse by 0.0172 BPB (bits per byte) and ran 15% slower, and its gradient came from a softmax-shaped surrogate. The starling read reached recall 0.329 where softmax reached 0.999. Both verdicts close those configurations only (decision D22), not the idea. See findings for the numbers and flock read for the discrete read that replaces them. What we know today: the best trained discrete model scored top-1 of 65 and 463 of 14,287 development rows, below a unigram count table (1,226) and a context-free successor table (6,300) ( measurement , K16 outcome ). The cause is open. The record rules out one suspect: aliasing did not explain the ranking failure. It leaves ranking capacity, the read, the address key and the training schedule.

540.body: UOR-R4 began in June 2026 as an attempt to run a language model without a transformer or heavy arithmetic, using the geometry of primes, rotations and symmetry groups. Over four months it tried five broad approaches. Each was replaced when it hit a wall, and each left lessons. The 32 steps below are the audit's "eras", read from the GitHub archive (items #1 to #2495 ). The work has been careful and open about its failures, and it has not yet produced a model that holds a conversation. A timeline from 10 June to 19 October 2026. A top band shows five phases, A to E, divided into 32 numbered eras. An area chart below shows catalog records per day, with nothing before 21 July and a peak of 74 on 13 October. 545.body: In plain words: replace softmax and matrix multiplication with true geometric operations, then learn on exact integers. Era Dates What was tried, and what happened 30 Mechanism rungs 10 to 13 Oct Softmax-free rank reads were REJECT ( #2160 ). Quaternion matrices and icosian weights were KEEP ( #2193 , #2216 ). The starling read lost entries to eviction at long context ( #2239 ) 31 Operator phase 12 to 14 Oct Softmax and matmul were banned ( #2251 , #2263 ). A rank-margin loss, the Hamilton gate and SpiralCore/FBS projection were added. Controls passed and nothing was trained 32 Discrete substrate 13 to 15 Oct Integer learning passed its CUDA controls ( #2379 ). The K16 runs then completed with no KEEP: the best top-1 was 65 and 463 of 14,287 rows, below a unigram table at 1,226 ( K16 outcome ). 554.body: Give the discrete model an attention-like read of context. Under the owner's rules (no softmax, no matrix multiplication, integer serving) the read must be a tree walk ( Route ), a small neighbour set rotated into the query's frame ( Flock ) or a link-following rule such as "the word after the earlier copy of this word" ( Relation ). The line's yardstick is milestone M1: a saved discrete artifact that, after export to integer serving and on each of two seeds, beats a unigram table and a successor table on the same development rows ( charter , item 8 of the research clauses).

555.body: Float readers and latches (19 Sep to 5 Oct). A hard capture-and-hold gate let saved models answer 128 of 128 original and stress rows, against 47 to 59 for same-size controls ( latch ). Fresh complete replies stayed low: a directed cue relation scored 0/32 and its cue-only control 1/32 ( cue carrier ). First integer GPU path (13 to 14 Oct). All eleven construction controls passed, then 25 of 25 ( discrete learning , driver cost ). The first training pilot (A2, 1,640 batches) raised top-1 from 17 to 82 and top-8 from 173 to 1,169 of 14,287, while the loss total rose from 13,816,032 to 13,884,032 ( pilot ). The diagnosis: the starting table had only 16 distinct vectors for 4,096 tokens ( diagnosis ). The admission wall (15 to 17 Oct). Re-scoring saved checkpoints with 8 to 16 kept cells never reached the 4,894 admission bar (best 2,400 at 16), so capacity had to be trained in ( sweep ). Repeated qualification restarts (five by the last record) stopped on build, interface and lint errors and then on a 99-against-100 timing count ( restart 5 ). A host check found that a context-free successor table already scores 6,300 of 14,287 ( host diagnostics ). Speed (16 to 18 Oct). In a three-batch diagnostic, over 99.99% of each proposal's time was one scoring kernel; a row-parallel version gave equal losses about 56 times faster (3.843 s to 0.0691 s) ( rows parity ). The paired test and the 16-cell runs (18 to 19 Oct). The first paired attention test (Dose 1) was stopped by the owner at 904 and 1,065 batches, before any checkpoint, to switch to the row-parallel driver (a diagnostic stop, not a verdict). The paired row-parallel run that followed (Dose 2) reached its registered collapse stop at 4,096 batches in both arms (the Relation read and a frozen control): admission on 3,847 copy-successor rows (development rows where copying the word after the previous occurrence would be right) fell from 2,034 to 225 (Relation) and 205 (frozen control) ( Q1 diagnosis ). Four runs of the 16-cell experiment (K16) used two training objectives, an address-margin loss (A) and an occupancy-rank loss (R), with two seeds each. They accepted 407, 130, 410 and 129 moves. The occupancy-rank loss collapsed to 19 or 20 occupied cells; the margin loss lost admission. Verdict: no KEEP (no run met its own target), and the fresh slice stays sealed ( outcome call ). Address cells (19 Oct). Placing each token's cell near its predecessors' cells lifted starting admission from 127 to 1,351 of 3,847 at zero training; a shuffled control got 476 ( pre-flight ). Training then eroded it in the address-cell dose (A8): Relation 1,351 to 551 (stopped), frozen control 857 ( A8 dose ). A controller that audits admission every 64 batches is built; its GPU qualification has not been run (NOT_RUN) ( controller ).

560.body: Replace the random start that caused the first pilot's ranking trouble. In that pilot the initializer produced only 16 distinct vectors for 4,096 token identities, so most words could not be told apart by the read ( A2 diagnosis ). The prime-zeta construction was registered as a zero-training check that a deterministic, arithmetic table could fix that.

560.title: What it set out to do

561.body: Token \(v\) gets the prime \(p_{\mathrm{id}(v)+1}\), so the vocabulary maps one to one onto the first \(V\) primes. For each of the first 512 pinned zeta-zero ordinates \(\gamma_k\), the phase is \(\theta_k(p)=\gamma_k\ln p \bmod 2\pi\). Four channels per 8-dimensional block are quantized to integers and matched to the nearest of 16 roots of the E8 lattice by an exact integer inner product. A word's writer cell is the pair of roots of its first and last block, a 16 by 16 grid of 256 cells with exactly 16 words each. A uniqueness pass then gives interior blocks distinct roots. Floating point appears only in this one-time host step (docs/labs/repo-renormalization-2026-10-19/audit/mechanisms/prime-zeta-codebook.json, field how_it_works).

562.body: Older reference work (undated). Replacing a stub router with sixteen zeta-window projections raised top-1 from 0.17 to 1.00, but only on a six-sentence fixture ( record ). An audit checked every consumer of the stored zeta state vector before widening its storage ( audit ). 14 Oct: construction qualified. The generator was built, with no training and no corpus rows. All 4,096 of 4,096 tokens receive unique vectors, 17 of 17 base CUDA controls and 6 of 6 prime-zeta controls pass, and the tables match across macOS and Linux ( construction record ). 18 to 19 Oct: used as a starting point. Starting from the injective table fixed aliasing but spread tokens over all 256 cells, so only 127 of 3,847 copy-successor rows had the right cell in view at 8 kept cells, below the 500 gate ( pre-flight ). Address-structured cells (see the M1 line ) lifted that to 1,351 at zero training, and prime-zeta remains the fallback inside that table.

567.body: Reach a first rule-compliant training result. The plan of 12 October named the pieces: a hard rank-hinge loss in place of cross-entropy, an exact flock selection on the 600-cell, a raw-score output head, a rotation gate in place of sigmoid gating and a geometric projection in place of dense maps ( design ). 568.body: September reviews. A frozen recurrent state added only 0.022 bits over a count table, so no readout work was justified ( result ). 11 Oct: the starling read. Trained from scratch, it scored mean recall 0.009 (chance 0.0045) where an L2-softmax control scored 0.617, because hard selection gives unchosen keys no gradient ( record ). A temporary dense helper raised the address hit rate from 10% to 73% but recall stayed at 0.011 ( anneal ). Gating by content instead of address did not help ( content ). 12 Oct: partial recoveries. A dense bootstrap teacher got 3 of 5 seeds to softmax-level recall, against 1 of 5 without it ( bootstrap ). A light distillation weight gave 0.380 ( sweep ). Training twice as long gave 0.78 on 5 of 5 seeds on a 512 synthetic test, a provisional KEEP (target met, at an unequal budget) ( recall ). At 1,536 context the read collapsed to 0.241 against 0.999, because each cell kept only its last four keys ( context ). A persistent tree fixed retention but recall stayed at 0.329 ( tree ). Quaternion weights (11 Oct). Quaternion-structured projections beat a dense model of equal parameters by 0.018 bits per byte, six times the noise, with four times fewer matrix weights than an equal-width dense model ( record ). 12 to 13 Oct: lawful rebuild. Source landed for the rank-hinge loss, the Hamilton gate, geometric recurrence gates and the SpiralCore and FBS projection. Finite GPU checks passed: 18 controls on the complete path ( rung 0 path ). No training followed. 13 Oct. The owner's D32 decision banned float model computation. The float qualification attempts were stopped and kept: 31 of 33 controls passed at the last complete replay; the 34-control replay was NOT_RUN. This was a scope change, not a mechanism negative ( record ).

574.body: September. Fifteen records dated 3 Sep are source audits and acceptance reviews of a text-to-clause adapter and a native bridge. A pre-registered exact-pair cache lowered the count reference by 0.238 bits per target on exposed project Markdown, not general prose ( result ). An always-on exact-store read failed its gate on all three seeds, with held-out accuracy of 0.03 to 0.16 against a 0.90 bar ( G1 ). A diagnostic put 77.7 percent of held-out failures at query-entity tagging ( decomposition ). 1 to 5 Oct. Adapting only the readouts raised complete own-prefix source replies from 4/20 to 18/20 ( coadapt ), yet a prospectively frozen fresh panel gave 0/8 ( frozen transfer ). 9 Oct. Traces showed why stored numbers failed. The copy pointer attended the repeated sentence frame, never the second digit of the value (0 of 13 rows), and the 4,096-piece vocabulary has no multi-digit tokens ( positional read ). Several attempts to build legal parameter changes with an exact solver stopped on numeric errors, which are blockers, not negatives. 10 Oct. Whole-answer replies on the 512-row development panel went 8, 22, 145, 175, 177, then 437 after training each token against its strongest wrong rival (260 gains and no losses on that last step) ( pooled rank ). Five other recipes lowered it (8 to 2, 8 to 4, 8 to 0 and 145 to 139 replies). The saved 437 model then scored 0/128 against a bar of 52 on fresh role and value combinations ( fresh ). 10 to 12 Oct. Training the read to land on the asked value was flat at first (19/40 against 20/40). A powered rerun over three seeds cut wrong-value failures from 47 to 30 of 120, and at four times the length from 49 to 23 ( scaled ). Both met their bars, so each was a KEEP (target met without a significant loss elsewhere), but on a softmax read. A whole-path source reference was built; CUDA execution has not been run (NOT_RUN) ( recovery ). The softmax ban (D23, 12 Oct) and the M2 training hold stopped further runs.

580.body: Design (14 Oct). Data is folded into hashed records that can be rebuilt or range-read with checks. A node id is 12 bytes. A 32,768-byte fixture record kept 70,972 bytes, a reminder that deduplication is not universal compression ( design ). Build (14 to 15 Oct). A Rust reader fetched 203 byte ranges with identical bytes from an eager and an indexed backend ( reader ). The store folded and rebuilt source bytes exactly; a repeated fixture kept 380 bytes for 7,776 raw bytes. Twenty integration tests and 13 tokenizer tests passed ( store ). Replication and audit (17 to 18 Oct). About 25 records add a peer protocol. A receiver holding an older 1 MiB version fetched 22 records, 1,014 bytes, in three rounds ( peer ). Batching a cold 52 MB pull over a high-latency link took 91.50 s against 236.19 s ( batch ). Pipelined fetches ran about 2.8 times faster with an emulated 8 ms delay, which is not a real wide-area measurement ( pipelined ). Other records add pinning, failover, repair, retries and a verified audit command. Twelve warm receivers pulling at once took 0.864 s against 3.506 s one at a time ( concurrency ). Second language (18 Oct). A pure-Python client audited and pulled a 256 KiB artifact from the Rust server over loopback, byte for byte ( conformance ). The test suite stands at 60 passing ( batch plumbing ).
